subject: FMHY P-Stream Forks category
claim: FMHY groups these entries as forks of P-Stream/movie-web and warns that default sources can differ. Category membership establishes FMHY's lineage classification, not identical runtime backends or common ownership.

The published architecture separates a static frontend, optional media proxy, account synchronization backend, and optional local extension/desktop component. These are distinct roles and are not interchangeable playback hosts.
The account backend is documented as synchronizing bookmarks, progress, history, groups and settings, with watch-party synchronization support. It is explicitly separate from media delivery.

The proxy documentation describes a stateless media-request component with distinct playlist, fragment, cache, quality and health routes. The production proxy origin and complete source-to-CDN chain are not established by those route descriptions.

AIOStreams documents aggregation of multiple Stremio addons and built-in source integrations, followed by deduplication, filtering, sorting and formatting. It supports distinct catalog, metadata, stream and subtitle functions and optional external media-proxy integrations. Its configured addons and deployment instance must be identified before attributing a final stream provider.

AIOMetadata documents movie, TV and anime metadata/artwork aggregation from TMDB, TVDB, MyAnimeList, AniList, IMDb, TVmaze, Fanart.tv and other sources. It separates configuration storage and caching from metadata delivery. Metadata and streaming-service catalog references do not themselves provide playable video.

The Stremio addon protocol exposes a manifest and typed resource routes. Catalog, detailed metadata, stream results and subtitles are distinct resources; an addon can implement only a subset. A manifest or catalog therefore cannot be treated as proof of direct media availability.

TMDB documents image URLs assembled from a configured image base, size and returned file path; its example uses image.tmdb.org/t/p. An image-host reference establishes artwork sourcing, not video hosting.

AniList's official documentation repository identifies its GraphQL API as powering AniList and AniChart. It points to graphql.anilist.co through its current interactive documentation link and marks older generated reference/editor links deprecated. This is a metadata/catalog API, not a video CDN.
